preamble: The shift from an alveolar or dental stop [d] to a retroflex stop (like [ɖ] or [ʈ]) typically occurs when the consonant is influenced by an adjacent rhotic sound [r] or through specific historical substrate influences. The tongue tip curls back further into the mouth.

examples.note: Supradental/retroflex assimilation: /r/ + /d/ cluster merges into a single voiced retroflex stop [ɖ] in connected speech.

sources: Fortson, B. W. (2010). Indo-European Language and Culture: An Introduction (2nd ed.). Wiley-Blackwell. https://www.wiley.com/en-us/Indo-European+Language+and+Culture%3A+An+Introduction%2C+2nd+Edition-p-9781405188968
